sources: admin-shim server.ts / lib/{runs,store,crons}.ts route inventory read on the 0.29.12 host (/opt/stacks/letta-code-parallel/admin-shim) — the per-method evidence for owner-vs-deny (lgns8.9)
rules: The presence of a native v2 command does not by itself transfer ownership; each app_server_v2 row is an explicit adoption decision scoped to a migration slice.

No operation may WRITE Letta durable storage directly. Reads may use the read-only local_backend_store tier ONLY where the App Server exposes no command and lettashim itself served the route by reading that same on-disk root; every write routes through a public contract (v2 protocol, bounded service adapter, or controller-owned state) so exactly one writer owns the backend root.
The Kotlin controller must not become admin-shim v2: admin_rest_service and vibesync_service rows are bounded injected adapters, not REST mirrors grown inside the fanout controller.
capability_gated_unsupported rows fail closed with an explicit capability error after cutover; they must never silently proxy.
production_first_route and current_backend describe observed production execution order; post_shim_owner/post_shim_fallback are cutover targets and must never be shim_until_cutover.

An unrouted_domains row that names shim_routes is a shim-only surface and must carry a disposition plus caller evidence; 'no caller found' is only a valid disposition when the evidence names the window it was measured over.
local_backend_store rows are READ-ONLY by construction and fail closed when LETTA_LOCAL_BACKEND_DIR is unset; they must never fall back to an HTTP admin host.

A capability_gated_unsupported row created by lgns8.9 must name, in its notes, both the admin-shim route that 404s today (proving the denial is parity, not a regression) and the UPSTREAM ASK that would lift it.
